Murfreesboro is the Rutherford County seat, 34 miles southeast of downtown Nashville. It had 171,178 residents by mid-2025, up from 152,769 in 2020. A sale touches three separate offices: the city's Tax Department, the Rutherford County Assessor and the county Register of Deeds.

The median owner-occupied home is valued at $402,100, and median gross rent is $1,481 a month. Owners live in 52.4 percent of homes, which leaves close to half rented or vacant, so tell a buyer early if tenants live in yours. Medians for the whole city only go so far. Closed sales near your address say more.

Bills for 2026 went out on October 1, 2026. The city charges no interest if payment arrives by February 28, 2027, and the same February 28 deadline applies every year from tax year 2025 forward. From March 1, unpaid base tax picks up 1.5 percent for each month or fraction. A postmark counts, and a weekend deadline rolls to the next day the city is open.

Ways to pay the Murfreesboro city bill

The city takes partial payments under set guidelines. Unpaid amounts go to Chancery Court at the proper deadline. The City Tax Department's number is (615) 893-5210.

Values come from the Rutherford County Assessor's Office, (615) 898-7750, and the city bills on those values. State law assesses residential property at 25 percent of appraised value. County boards of equalization convene each June 1, so ask the assessor for this year's appeal deadline.

The city takes part in Tennessee's Property Tax Freeze and Property Tax Relief programs for low-income seniors 65 and older and for qualifying disabled owners. If you are enrolled, ask the City Tax Department how a sale affects your application before you list.

Back taxes do not block a sale. The title company asks the City Tax Department for a payoff, and whatever is unpaid comes out of your proceeds at closing. If a balance has already gone to Chancery Court, tell the title agent right away, since that changes who must be paid and when.

Building and Codes works under the 2024 building codes and covers plan review, inspections and certificates of occupancy. Inspectors take questions at the office early each morning before they head to job sites, and the front counter stops taking money at 4:00 p.m. The City Council also keeps a schedule of development impact fees.

Short-term rental owners pay a 5 percent occupancy tax monthly to the county and city, plus state business and sales tax. They also need a business license from the county clerk and the city, $15 each. Airbnb and VRBO hosts are included. If your house hosts guests, give the buyer the license records.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Rutherford County
sections.html:
The recording office is Room 133 at 319 North Maple Street. Its posted policy says a document paid $10 or less over the required fee is recorded and the extra is kept, while overpayments above $10 are refunded by check at the end of the month. A document short on fees comes back the same day.

The buyer, as grantee, pays Tennessee's transfer tax at recording, which works out to 37 cents per $100.

On April 10, 2009, a low-end EF4 tornado struck the fringes of the city, killing two people and injuring 41. It destroyed 117 homes and heavily damaged 292. Buyers in older parts of town may ask whether a house was repaired after a storm. If you replaced a roof or rebuilt after storm damage, keep invoices and permit numbers together to hand over.

1. Describe the house, and mention any tenants.
  2. A buyer sends an offer, and you accept it.
  3. The title company gets a payoff from the City Tax Department and checks the county records.
  4. You sign the deed, the grantee's side pays the transfer tax, and the deed is recorded on North Maple Street.
  5. Back taxes and any mortgage balance are paid from your proceeds.

A cash purchase has no lender, so the closing waits on title work and not on a bank appraisal. That helps when a move date is fixed or a rental is sitting empty.

faqs.q: When do Murfreesboro city taxes stop being interest-free?
faqs.a: After February 28 each year. For the 2026 tax year, interest starts March 1, 2027, at 1.5 percent per month or part of a month on unpaid base tax. A weekend deadline moves to the next working day.

faqs.q: Can I pay Murfreesboro city taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Partial payments are accepted under the city's guidelines. Unpaid amounts are turned over to Chancery Court at the proper deadline, so call (615) 893-5210 first.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Murfreesboro assessment?
faqs.a: The Rutherford County Assessor's Office at (615) 898-7750. Payment and tax relief questions go to the City Tax Department at (615) 893-5210.

faqs.q: Is there property tax help for seniors in Murfreesboro?
faqs.a: Yes. The city participates in Tennessee's Property Tax Freeze and Property Tax Relief programs for qualifying low-income owners 65 and older and for qualifying disabled owners.

faqs.q: What do short-term rental owners owe in Murfreesboro?
faqs.a: A 5 percent occupancy tax paid monthly to the county and city, state sales tax and gross receipts business tax, and $15 business licenses from the county clerk and the city.
